label: The advisor routes off three representations (compiled skill-graph.json, SQLite node table, on-disk graph-metadata); the canonical reindex is operator-gated and the freshness panel is report-only, always exit 0.
Live: compiled skill-graph.json is STALE (generated 2026-10-02 vs newest source stamp 2026-10-04, cli-classifier); no zombie/ghost/missing nodes.
The freshness panel is wired only to a doctor route; neither CI nor hooks run it, so a stale compiled graph passes every check that does run.
Parent-skill-check 5k enforces lexical agreement between alias/class keywords, packet names/description keywords and canary coverage, with per-hub warn-only legs — coherence, never reach.
The only end-to-end reach prober asks the advisor per phrase and is wired to a doctor route only; it is the sole check that can see 'edit landed but did not take effect'.

Root cause second half: an author edit must traverse two operator-gated reindexes before the served scorer sees it, while every fast check compares surfaces to each other or requires the reindex to have run.

Smallest fix: expose staleness by flipping the panel to a gateable exit and wiring it plus the intent-signals check into the existing routing-drift job; extend the carry generator to source description.json keywords so the author's file becomes effective; name the reindex command in failures.
Negatives: try values first (intent signals for the expected winners) before an anti-signal lane; an anti-signal lane is a new scorer lane and must land in the served implementation.
Proof set: freshness panel, generate-router-intent-signals --check, and the advisor battery replay — today: STALE, FAILED (23 missing), 13/17 and 2/5.
